summary: Agent-visible bootstrap contract for loading bounded Shin context from undocumented, source-only, mixed-language, documentation-only, or empty repositories without mutating the consumer.
goal: An agent entering an unfamiliar repository can discover Shin globally, classify available evidence, build an external deterministic index, and request a bounded brief before broad scanning.

architectureBoundary.reason: Bootstrap profiles reuse bounded language declaration extraction and point agents to primary source files; Shin is not a compiler, type checker, LSP, or full call-graph engine.
architectureBoundary.sourceAuthority: Generated context is retrieval evidence. Source documents, code, tests, and accepted decisions remain authoritative.

states.empty: No recognized source family or indexable project documentation exists; build metadata alone remains a structural signal and does not promise retrievable context.
states.source-only: Supported source or build metadata exists without product documentation; documentation is not required for bootstrap.
states.documented: Project documentation or a root README exists and can be combined with recognized source facts.

emptyBehavior.nextAction: Add source code or machine documentation, then rerun discover.

bootstrapProfiles.evidence: Java source plus optional Maven and Gradle root metadata
Kotlin source plus optional Maven, Gradle, and Kotlin DSL root metadata
TypeScript and JavaScript source plus optional package and compiler metadata
C, C++, Objective-C and Objective-C++ source plus optional CMake and Make metadata
C# source plus optional .NET root metadata
Retool apps, resources, workflows, RSX, payloads, bindings, and workflow edges
Mixed Java, Kotlin, C#, TypeScript, JavaScript and C-family source trees, including Objective-C/Objective-C++
README, AGENTS, and docs tree when no supported source family is recognized

profileContract.rootFiles: Required project-specific entry files; may be empty when other inputs are configured.
profileContract.optionalRootFiles: Conventional root metadata included only when present; missing candidates are not errors.
profileContract.sourceFactRoots: May independently back a fact-only index without source documents; missing conventional roots are informational for bootstrapOnly profiles while permanent profiles retain strict warnings.
profileContract.bootstrapOnly: Marks a generic discovery profile that intentionally has no project-specific golden eval cases.
profileContract.strictProfileCheck: Bootstrap profiles pass strict profile-check with an informational bootstrap-profile-without-eval issue.
profileContract.bootstrapLinkPolicy: bootstrapOnly profiles publish broken local links as diagnostics so an imperfect unfamiliar repository remains retrievable; permanent profiles reject the same candidate snapshot.
profileContract.doctorPolicy: Bootstrap uses non-strict doctor and requires zero errors while surfacing warnings. doctor --strict intentionally fails when diagnostic warnings remain and is mandatory after permanent adoption.
profileContract.evalBoundary: Do not run eval --strict for bootstrap-only profiles. Permanent adoption requires a consumer profile with golden evalCases.

safeTraversal.symlinkPolicy: Profile inputs, optional roots, source roots, agent start paths, recursive source files, and discovery signals fail closed or are skipped when the entry or any relative ancestor is a symlink; lexical parent traversal is rejected.
safeTraversal.caps: Profiles bound candidate file count and per-file bytes; strict doctor reports caps or unsupported empty input.

agentWorkflow: Locate Shin through the global shin-context Codex skill.
Check only conventional AGENTS and Shin adoption marker paths; an adopted consumer profile takes precedence over generic bootstrap.
Run make in the Shin repository so the binary matches source and VERSION.
Run discover against the consumer root and trust bootstrap.primary_profile.
Run profile-check --strict with the selected generic profile.
Build into a Shin-owned build/context/bootstrap/<consumer-name> out directory.
Run check and non-strict doctor; require zero errors and surface every warning.
Run brief <task-query> --projection compact --require-current before broad source scans.
Open only returned primary source paths needed to verify important claims.

codexSkill.officialValidation: Codex skill-creator quick_validate.py passed against canonical and installed copies on M4.
codexSkill.implicitTrigger: Unknown, undocumented, source-only, newly created, or documentation-heavy repository before broad scanning.

planner.authority: Lifecycle readiness only; adoption-check --strict remains the marker validator.

promotionRequirements: agentStartPaths when stable entry documents exist
project-local shin.project-adoption.v1 marker only when explicitly adopted

adoptionPrecedence.rule: An explicit project-local Shin adoption marker takes precedence over discovery bootstrap profiles.

hermeticEvidence.partialLayoutEvidence: A Retool repository containing apps without resources or workflows passes strict profile bootstrap and reports missing conventional roots as informational.
hermeticEvidence.imperfectDocumentationEvidence: A bootstrap docs corpus with a broken local link publishes a current diagnostic snapshot, passes non-strict doctor with zero errors, fails strict doctor on the warning, and remains queryable with --require-current.
hermeticEvidence.localServiceDocumentationPolicy: Local bootstrap qualification accepts only a link-only strict doctor or vacuum failure when errors, other warnings, generated drift and unfinished changes are absent. Strict Core audit results and explicit permanent-profile gates remain unchanged. Service status exposes a bounded documentation_warnings count; Monitor and TUI explain the warning while serving verified context and clear it after a qualified correction.

nonGoals: No complete language grammar or standard-library model.
No type checking, compilation, runtime execution, or complete call graph.
No automatic documentation generation or consumer mutation during bootstrap.
No claim of project-specific retrieval quality until a promoted profile defines evalCases.
